title: Little Bo-Peep
text:
Little Bo-Peep has lost her sheep,
And can't tell where to find them;
Leave them alone, and they'll come home,
And bring their tails behind them.

Little Bo-Peep fell fast asleep,
And dreamt she heard them bleating;
But when she awoke, she found it a joke,
For still they all were fleeting.

Then up she took her little crook,
Determined for to find them;
She found them indeed, but it made her heart bleed,
For they'd left all their tails behind 'em!

It happened one day, as Bo-peep did stray
Unto a meadow hard by--
There she espied their tails, side by side,
All hung on a tree to dry.

She heaved a sigh and wiped her eye,
And over the hillocks she raced;
And tried what she could, as a shepherdess should,
That each tail should be properly placed.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose or the Old Nursery Rhymes, ill. Kate Greenaway (Warne) (1881)

title: Little Boy Blue
text:
Little Boy Blue, come, blow your horn!
The sheep's in the meadow, the cow's in the corn.
Where's the little boy that looks after the sheep?
Under the haystack, fast asleep!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: The Clock
text:
There's a neat little clock,--
In the schoolroom it stands,--
And it points to the time
With its two little hands.

And may we, like the clock,
Keep a face clean and bright,
With hands ever ready
To do what is right.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Winter
text:
Cold and raw the north wind doth blow,
Bleak in the morning early;
All the hills are covered with snow,
And winter's now come fairly.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: A Seasonable Song
text:
Piping hot, smoking hot.
What I've got
You have not.
Hot gray pease, hot, hot, hot;
Hot gray pease, hot.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Three Children On The Ice
text:
Three children sliding on the ice
Upon a summer's day,
As it fell out, they all fell in,
The rest they ran away.

Oh, had these children been at school,
Or sliding on dry ground,
Ten thousand pounds to one penny
They had not then been drowned.

Ye parents who have children dear,
And ye, too, who have none,
If you would keep them safe abroad
Pray keep them safe at home.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)

title: Cross Patch
text:
Cross patch, draw the latch,
Sit by the fire and spin;
Take a cup and drink it up,
Then call your neighbors in.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose or the Old Nursery Rhymes, ill. Kate Greenaway (Warne) (1881)
Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)

title: The Old Woman Under A Hill
text:
There was an old woman
Lived under a hill;
And if she's not gone,
She lives there still.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose or the Old Nursery Rhymes, ill. Kate Greenaway (Warne) (1881)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Tweedle-Dum And Tweedle-Dee
text:
Tweedle-dum and Tweedle-dee
Resolved to have a battle,
For Tweedle-dum said Tweedle-dee
Had spoiled his nice new rattle.

Just then flew by a monstrous crow,
As big as a tar barrel,
Which frightened both the heroes so,
They quite forgot their quarrel.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Oh, Dear!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Little Jumping Joan
text:
Here am I, little jumping Joan,
When nobody's with me
I'm always alone.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose or the Old Nursery Rhymes, ill. Kate Greenaway (Warne) (1881)
Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Pat-A-Cake
text:
Pat-a-cake, pat-a-cake,
Baker's man!
So I do, master,
As fast as I can.

Pat it, and prick it,
And mark it with T,
Put it in the oven
For Tommy and me.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Money And The Mare
text:
"Lend me thy mare to ride a mile."
"She is lamed, leaping over a stile."

"Alack! and I must keep the fair!
I'll give thee money for thy mare."

"Oh, oh! say you so?
Money will make the mare to go!"
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Robin Redbreast
text:
Little Robin Redbreast sat upon a tree,
Up went Pussy-Cat, down went he,
Down came Pussy-Cat, away Robin ran,
Says little Robin Redbreast: "Catch me if you can!"

Little Robin Redbreast jumped upon a spade,
Pussy-Cat jumped after him, and then he was afraid.
Little Robin chirped and sang, and what did Pussy say?
Pussy-Cat said: "Mew, mew, mew," and Robin flew away.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: A Melancholy Song
text:
Trip upon trenchers,
And dance upon dishes,
My mother sent me for some barm, some barm;
She bid me go lightly,
And come again quickly,
For fear the young men should do me some harm.
Yet didn't you see, yet didn't you see,
What naughty tricks they put upon me?
They broke my pitcher
And spilt the water,
And huffed my mother,
And chid her daughter,
And kissed my sister instead of me.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)

title: Jack
text:
Jack be nimble, Jack be quick,
Jack jump over the candlestick.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)

title: Going To St. Ives
text:
As I was going to St. Ives
I met a man with seven wives.
Every wife had seven sacks,
Every sack had seven cats,
Every cat had seven kits.
Kits, cats, sacks, and wives,
How many were going to St. Ives?
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Thirty Days Hath September
text:
Thirty days hath September,
April, June, and November;
February has twenty-eight alone,
All the rest have thirty-one,
Excepting leap-year, that's the time
When February's days are twenty-nine.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Baby Dolly
text:
Hush, baby, my dolly, I pray you don't cry,
And I'll give you some bread, and some milk by-and-by;
Or perhaps you like custard, or, maybe, a tart,
Then to either you're welcome, with all my heart.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Come Out To Play
text:
Girls and boys, come out to play,
The moon doth shine as bright as day;
Leave your supper, and leave your sleep,
And come with your playfellows into the street.
Come with a whoop, come with a call,
Come with a good will or not at all.
Up the ladder and down the wall,
A half-penny roll will serve us all.
You find milk, and I'll find flour,
And we'll have a pudding in half an hour.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: If Wishes Were Horses
text:
If wishes were horses, beggars would ride.
If turnips were watches, I would wear one by my side.
And if "ifs" and "ands"
Were pots and pans,
There'd be no work for tinkers!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: To Market
text:
To market, to market, to buy a fat pig.
Home again, home again, jiggety jig.
To market, to market, to buy a fat hog,
Home again, home again, jiggety jog.
To market, to market, to buy a plum bun,
Home again, home again, market is done.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)

title: Old Chairs To Mend
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Robin And Richard
text:
Robin and Richard were two pretty men,
They lay in bed till the clock struck ten;
Then up starts Robin and looks at the sky,
"Oh, brother Richard, the sun's very high!
You go before, with the bottle and bag,
And I will come after on little Jack Nag."
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: A Man And A Maid
text:
There was a little man,
Who wooed a little maid,
And he said, "Little maid, will you wed, wed, wed?
I have little more to say,
So will you, yea or nay,
For least said is soonest mended-ded, ded, ded."

The little maid replied,
"Should I be your little bride,
Pray what must we have for to eat, eat, eat?
Will the flame that you're so rich in
Light a fire in the kitchen?
Or the little god of love turn the spit, spit, spit?"
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Clever Hen
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Two Birds
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Leg Over Leg
text:
Leg over leg,
As the dog went to Dover;
When he came to a stile,
Jump, he went over.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: When Jenny Wren Was Young
text:
'Twas once upon a time, when Jenny Wren was young,
So daintily she danced and so prettily she sung,
Robin Redbreast lost his heart, for he was a gallant bird.
So he doffed his hat to Jenny Wren, requesting to be heard.

"Oh, dearest Jenny Wren, if you will but be mine,
You shall feed on cherry pie and drink new currant wine,
I'll dress you like a goldfinch or any peacock gay,
So, dearest Jen, if you'll be mine, let us appoint the day."

Jenny blushed behind her fan and thus declared her mind:
"Since, dearest Bob, I love you well, I'll take your offer kind.
Cherry pie is very nice and so is currant wine,
But I must wear my plain brown gown and never go too fine."
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)

title: Barber
text:
Barber, barber, shave a pig.
How many hairs will make a wig?
Four and twenty; that's enough.
Give the barber a pinch of snuff.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: The Flying Pig
text:
Dickory, dickory, dare,
The pig flew up in the air;
The man in brown soon brought
him down,
Dickory,
dickory,
dare.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Solomon Grundy
text:
Solomon Grundy,
Born on a Monday,
Christened on Tuesday,
Married on Wednesday,
Took ill on Thursday,
Worse on Friday,
Died on Saturday,
Buried on Sunday.
This is the end
Of Solomon Grundy.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Hush-A-Bye
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Burnie Bee
text:
Burnie bee, burnie bee,
Tell me when your wedding be?
If it be to-morrow day,
Take your wings and fly away.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: The Hunter Of Reigate
text:
A man went a-hunting at Reigate,
And wished to leap over a high gate.
Says the owner, "Go round,
With your gun and your hound,
For you never shall leap over my gate."
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Ride Away, Ride Away
text:
Ride away, ride away,
Johnny shall ride,
And he shall have pussy-cat
Tied to one side;
And he shall have little dog
Tied to the other,
And Johnny shall ride
To see his grandmother.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)

title: Pussy-Cat And Queen
text:
"Pussy-cat, pussy-cat,
Where have you been?"
"I've been to London
To look at the Queen."

"Pussy-cat, pussy-cat,
What did you there?"
"I frightened a little mouse
Under the chair."
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Christmas
text:
Christmas comes but once a year,
And when it comes it brings good cheer.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Heigh-Ho, The Carrion Crow
text:
A carrion crow sat on an oak,
Fol de riddle, lol de riddle, hi ding do,
Watching a tailor shape his cloak;
Sing heigh-ho, the carrion crow,
Fol de riddle, lol de riddle, hi ding do!

Wife, bring me my old bent bow,
Fol de riddle, lol de riddle, hi ding do,
That I may shoot yon carrion crow;
Sing heigh-ho, the carrion crow,
Fol de riddle, lol de riddle, hi ding do!

The tailor he shot, and missed his mark,
Fol de riddle, lol de riddle, hi ding do!
And shot his own sow quite through the heart;
Sing heigh-ho, the carrion crow,
Fol de riddle, lol de riddle, hi ding do!

Wife! bring brandy in a spoon,
Fol de riddle, lol de riddle, hi ding do!
For our old sow is in a swoon;
Sing heigh-ho, the carrion crow,
Fol de riddle, lol de riddle, hi ding do!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Abc
text:
Great A, little a,
Bouncing B!
The cat's in the cupboard,
And can't see me.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: A Needle And Thread
text:
Old Mother Twitchett had but one eye,
And a long tail which she let fly;
And every time she went through a gap,
A bit of her tail she left in a trap.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Banbury Cross
text:
Ride a cock-horse to Banbury Cross,
To see an old lady upon a white horse.
Rings on her fingers, and bells on her toes,
She shall have music wherever she goes.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Man In Our Town
text:
There was a man in our town,
And he was wondrous wise,
He jumped into a bramble bush,
And scratched out both his eyes;
But when he saw his eyes were out,
With all his might and main,
He jumped into another bush,
And scratched 'em in again.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)

title: Georgy Porgy
text:
Georgy Porgy, pudding and pie,
Kissed the girls and made them cry.
When the boys came out to play,
Georgy Porgy ran away.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose or the Old Nursery Rhymes, ill. Kate Greenaway (Warne) (1881)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: For Every Evil
text:
For every evil under the sun
There is a remedy or there is none.
If there be one, seek till you find it;
If there be none, never mind it.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Cushy Cow
text:
Cushy cow, bonny, let down thy milk,
And I will give thee a gown of silk;
A gown of silk and a silver tee,
If thou wilt let down thy milk to me.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Wee Willie Winkie
text:
Wee Willie Winkie runs through the town,
Upstairs and downstairs, in his nightgown;
Rapping at the window, crying through the lock,
"Are the children in their beds? Now it's eight o'clock."
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)

title: About The Bush
text:
About the bush, Willie,
About the beehive,
About the bush, Willie,
I'll meet thee alive.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: See-Saw
text:
See-saw, Margery Daw,
Sold her bed and lay upon straw.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: John Smith
text:
Is John Smith within?
Yes, that he is.
Can he set a shoe?
Ay, marry, two.
Here a nail, there a nail,
Tick, tack, too.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Simple Simon
text:
Simple Simon met a pieman,
Going to the fair;
Says Simple Simon to the pieman,
"Let me taste your ware."

Says the pieman to Simple Simon,
"Show me first your penny,"
Says Simple Simon to the pieman,
"Indeed, I have not any."

Simple Simon went a-fishing
For to catch a whale;
All the water he could find
Was in his mother's pail!

Simple Simon went to look
If plums grew on a thistle;
He pricked his fingers very much,
Which made poor Simon whistle.

He went to catch a dicky bird,
And thought he could not fail,
Because he had a little salt,
To put upon its tail.

He went for water with a sieve,
But soon it ran all through;
And now poor Simple Simon
Bids you all adieu.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)

title: Three Blind Mice
text:
Three blind mice! See how they run!
They all ran after the farmer's wife,
Who cut off their tails with a carving knife.
Did you ever see such a thing in your life
As three blind mice?
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: A Little Man
text:
There was a little man, and he had a little gun,
And his bullets were made of lead, lead, lead;
He went to the brook, and saw a little duck,
And shot it right through the head, head, head.

He carried it home to his old wife Joan,
And bade her a fire to make, make, make.
To roast the little duck he had shot in the brook,
And he'd go and fetch the drake, drake, drake.

The drake was a-swimming with his curly tail;
The little man made it his mark, mark, mark.
He let off his gun, but he fired too soon,
And the drake flew away with a quack, quack, quack.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Diddle Diddle Dumpling
text:
Diddle diddle dumpling, my son John
Went to bed with his breeches on,
One stocking off, and one stocking on;
Diddle diddle dumpling, my son John.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)

title: Jerry Hall
text:
Jerry Hall, he was so small,
A rat could eat him, hat and all.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Black Hen
text:
Hickety, pickety, my black hen,
She lays eggs for gentlemen;
Gentlemen come every day
To see what my black hen doth lay.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: A Candle
text:
Little Nanny Etticoat
In a white petticoat,
And a red nose;
The longer she stands
The shorter she grows.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)

title: Miss Muffet
text:
Little Miss Muffet
Sat on a tuffet,
Eating of curds and whey;
There came a big spider,
And sat down beside her,
And frightened Miss Muffet away.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose or the Old Nursery Rhymes, ill. Kate Greenaway (Warne) (1881)
Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)

title: Curly-Locks
text:
Curly-locks, Curly-locks, wilt thou be mine?
Thou shalt not wash the dishes, nor yet feed the swine;
But sit on a cushion, and sew a fine seam
And feed upon strawberries, sugar, and cream.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Humpty Dumpty
text:
Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall,
Humpty Dumpty had a great fall;
All the King's horses, and all the King's men
Cannot put Humpty Dumpty together again.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose or the Old Nursery Rhymes, ill. Kate Greenaway (Warne) (1881)
Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)

title: One, Two, Three
text:
One, two, three, four, five,
Once I caught a fish alive.
Six, seven, eight, nine, ten,
But I let it go again.
Why did you let it go?
Because it bit my finger so.
Which finger did it bite?
The little one upon the right.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Dove And The Wren
text:
The dove says coo, coo, what shall I do?
I can scarce maintain two.
Pooh, pooh! says the wren, I've got ten,
And keep them all like gentlemen.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Master I Have
text:
Master I have, and I am his man,
Gallop a dreary dun;
Master I have, and I am his man,
And I'll get a wife as fast as I can;
With a heighty gaily gamberally,
Higgledy piggledy, niggledy, niggledy,
Gallop a dreary dun.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Pins
text:
See a pin and pick it up,
All the day you'll have good luck.
See a pin and let it lay,
Bad luck you'll have all the day.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Shall We Go A-Shearing?
text:
"Old woman, old woman, shall we go a-shearing?"
"Speak a little louder, sir, I am very thick of hearing."
"Old woman, old woman, shall I kiss you dearly?"
"Thank you, kind sir, I hear you very clearly."
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)

title: Goosey, Goosey, Gander
text:
Goosey, goosey, gander,
Whither dost thou wander?
Upstairs and downstairs
And in my lady's chamber.

There I met an old man
Who wouldn't say his prayers;
I took him by the left leg,
And threw him down the stairs.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Cock And The Hen
text:
"Cock, cock, cock, cock,
I've laid an egg,
Am I to gang ba--are-foot?"

"Hen, hen, hen, hen,
I've been up and down
To every shop in town,
And cannot find a shoe
To fit your foot,
If I'd crow my hea--art out."
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)

title: Blue Bell Boy
text:
I had a little boy,
And called him Blue Bell;
Gave him a little work,--
He did it very well.

I bade him go upstairs
To bring me a gold pin;
In coal scuttle fell he,
Up to his little chin.

He went to the garden
To pick a little sage;
He tumbled on his nose,
And fell into a rage.

He went to the cellar
To draw a little beer;
And quickly did return
To say there was none there.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Why May Not I Love Johnny?
text:
Johnny shall have a new bonnet,
And Johnny shall go to the fair,
And Johnny shall have a blue ribbon
To tie up his bonny brown hair.

And why may not I love Johnny?
And why may not Johnny love me?
And why may not I love Johnny
As well as another body?

And here's a leg for a stocking,
And here's a foot for a shoe,
And he has a kiss for his daddy,
And two for his mammy, I trow.

And why may not I love Johnny?
And why may not Johnny love me?
And why may not I love Johnny
As well as another body?
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose or the Old Nursery Rhymes, ill. Kate Greenaway (Warne) (1881)
The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Jack Jelf
text:
Little Jack Jelf
Was put on the shelf
Because he could not spell "pie";
When his aunt, Mrs. Grace,
Saw his sorrowful face,
She could not help saying, "Oh, fie!"

And since Master Jelf
Was put on the shelf
Because he could not spell "pie,"
Let him stand there so grim,
And no more about him,
For I wish him a very good-bye!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Hush-A-Bye
text:
Hush-a-bye, baby,
Daddy is near;
Mamma is a lady,
And that's very clear.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Girl In The Lane
text:
The girl in the lane, that couldn't speak plain,
Cried, "Gobble, gobble, gobble":
The man on the hill that couldn't stand still,
Went hobble hobble, hobble.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Hush-A-Bye
text:
Hush-a-bye, baby, lie still with thy daddy,
Thy mammy has gone to the mill,
To get some meal to bake a cake,
So pray, my dear baby, lie still.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Nancy Dawson
text:
Nancy Dawson was so fine
She wouldn't get up to serve the swine;
She lies in bed till eight or nine,
So it's Oh, poor Nancy Dawson.

And do ye ken Nancy Dawson, honey?
The wife who sells the barley, honey?
She won't get up to feed her swine,
And do ye ken Nancy Dawson, honey?
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Handy Pandy
text:
Handy Pandy, Jack-a-dandy,
Loves plum cake and sugar candy.
He bought some at a grocer's shop,
And out he came, hop, hop, hop!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Jack And Jill
text:
Jack and Jill went up the hill,
To fetch a pail of water;
Jack fell down, and broke his crown,
And Jill came tumbling after.

Then up Jack got and off did trot,
As fast as he could caper,
To old Dame Dob, who patched his nob
With vinegar and brown paper.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: The Alphabet
text:
A, B, C, and D,
Pray, playmates, agree.
E, F, and G,
Well, so it shall be.
J, K, and L,
In peace we will dwell.
M, N, and O,
To play let us go.
P, Q, R, and S,
Love may we possess.
W, X, and Y,
Will not quarrel or die.
Z, and ampersand,
Go to school at command.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Dance To Your Daddie
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: One Misty Moisty Morning
text:
One misty moisty morning,
When cloudy was the weather,
I chanced to meet an old man,
Clothed all in leather.
He began to compliment
And I began to grin.
How do you do? And how do you do?
And how do you do again?
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)

title: Robin Hood And Little John
text:
Robin Hood, Robin Hood,
Is in the mickle wood!
Little John, Little John,
He to the town is gone.

Robin Hood, Robin Hood,
Telling his beads,
All in the greenwood
Among the green weeds.

Little John, Little John,
If he comes no more,
Robin Hood, Robin Hood,
We shall fret full sore!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Old Woman From France
text:
There came an old woman from France
Who taught grown-up children to dance;
But they were so stiff,
She sent them home in a sniff,
This sprightly old woman from France.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Teeth And Gums
text:
Thirty white horses upon a red hill,
Now they tramp, now they champ, now they stand still.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: The Robins
text:
A robin and a robin's son
Once went to town to buy a bun.
They couldn't decide on plum or plain,
And so they went back home again.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: T'Other Little Tune
text:
I won't be my father's Jack,
I won't be my father's Jill;
I will be the fiddler's wife,
And have music when I will.
T'other little tune,
T'other little tune,
Prithee, Love, play me
T'other little tune.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)

title: My Kitten
text:
Hey, my kitten, my kitten,
And hey, my kitten, my deary!
Such a sweet pet as this
Was neither far nor neary.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Pancake Day
text:
Great A, little a,
This is pancake day;
Toss the ball high,
Throw the ball low,
Those that come after
May sing heigh-ho!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: A Plum Pudding
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Forehead, Eyes, Cheeks, Nose, Mouth, And Chin
text:
Here sits the Lord Mayor,
Here sit his two men,
Here sits the cock,
Here sits the hen,
Here sit the little chickens,
Here they run in.
Chin-chopper, chin-chopper, chin chopper, chin!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Two Pigeons
text:
I had two pigeons bright and gay,
They flew from me the other day.
What was the reason they did go?
I cannot tell, for I do not know.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: A Sure Test
text:
If you are to be a gentleman,
As I suppose you'll be,
You'll neither laugh nor smile,
For a tickling of the knee.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Lion And The Unicorn
text:
The Lion and the Unicorn were fighting for the crown,
The Lion beat the Unicorn all around the town.
Some gave them white bread, and some gave them brown,
Some gave them plum-cake, and sent them out of town.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: I Had A Little Husband
text:
I had a little husband no bigger than my thumb,
I put him in a pint pot, and there I bid him drum,
I bought a little handkerchief to wipe his little nose,
And a pair of little garters to tie his little hose.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)

title: To Babylon
text:
How many miles is it to Babylon?--
Threescore miles and ten.
Can I get there by candle-light?--
Yes, and back again.
If your heels are nimble and light,
You may get there by candle-light.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)

title: I'Ll Tell You A Story
text:
I'll tell you a story
About Jack-a-Nory:
And now my story's begun.
I'll tell you another
About his brother:
And now my story is done.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: A Strange Old Woman
text:
There was an old woman, and what do you think?
She lived upon nothing but victuals and drink;
Victuals and drink were the chief of her diet,
And yet this old woman could never be quiet.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)

title: Sleep, Baby, Sleep
text:
Sleep, baby, sleep,
Our cottage vale is deep:
The little lamb is on the green,
With woolly fleece so soft and clean--
Sleep, baby, sleep.
Sleep, baby, sleep,
Down where the woodbines creep;
Be always like the lamb so mild,
A kind, and sweet, and gentle child.
Sleep, baby, sleep.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Cry, Baby
text:
Cry, baby, cry,
Put your finger in your eye,
And tell your mother it wasn't I.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Baa, Baa, Black Sheep
text:
Baa, baa, black sheep,
Have you any wool?
Yes, marry, have I,
Three bags full;

One for my master,
One for my dame,
But none for the little boy
Who cries in the lane.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Little Fred
text:
When little Fred went to bed,
He always said his prayers;

He kissed mamma, and then papa,
And straightway went upstairs.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Cat And The Fiddle
text:
Hey, diddle, diddle!
The cat and the fiddle,
The cow jumped over the moon;
The little dog laughed
To see such sport,
And the dish ran away with the spoon.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Doctor Fell
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Jack And His Fiddle
text:
"Jacky, come and give me thy fiddle,
If ever thou mean to thrive."
"Nay, I'll not give my fiddle
To any man alive.

"If I should give my fiddle,
They'll think that I've gone mad;
For many a joyous day
My fiddle and I have had."
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Buttons
text:
Buttons, a farthing a pair!
Come, who will buy them of me?
They're round and sound and pretty,
And fit for girls of the city.
Come, who will buy them of me?
Buttons, a farthing a pair!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Little Pussy
text:
I like little Pussy,
Her coat is so warm,

And if I don't hurt her
She'll do me no harm;

So I'll not pull her tail,
Nor drive her away,

But Pussy and I
Very gently will play.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Sing A Song Of Sixpence
text:
Sing a song of sixpence,
A pocket full of rye;
Four-and-twenty blackbirds
Baked in a pie!

When the pie was opened
The birds began to sing;
Was not that a dainty dish
To set before the king?

The king was in his counting-house,
Counting out his money;
The queen was in the parlor,
Eating bread and honey.

The maid was in the garden,
Hanging out the clothes;
When down came a blackbird
And snapped off her nose.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Derby Ram
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Hobby-Horse
text:
I had a little hobby-horse,
And it was dapple gray;
Its head was made of pea-straw,
Its tail was made of hay.

I sold it to an old woman
For a copper groat;
And I'll not sing my song again
Without another coat.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Young Lambs To Sell
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Boy And The Sparrow
text:
A little cock-sparrow sat on a green tree,
And he chirruped, he chirruped, so merry was he;
A naughty boy came with his wee bow and arrow,
Determined to shoot this little cock-sparrow.

"This little cock-sparrow shall make me a stew,
And his giblets shall make me a little pie, too."
"Oh, no," says the sparrow "I won't make a stew."
So he flapped his wings and away he flew.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Old Woman, Old Woman
text:
There was an old woman tossed in a basket,
Seventeen times as high as the moon;
But where she was going no mortal could tell,
For under her arm she carried a broom.

"Old woman, old woman, old woman," said I,
"Whither, oh whither, oh whither so high?"
"To sweep the cobwebs from the sky;
And I'll be with you by-and-by."
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The First Of May
text:
The fair maid who, the first of May,
Goes to the fields at break of day,
And washes in dew from the hawthorn-tree,
Will ever after handsome be.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Sulky Sue
text:
Here's Sulky Sue,
What shall we do?
Turn her face to the wall
Till she comes to.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Little Jenny Wren
text:
Little Jenny Wren fell sick,
Upon a time;
In came Robin Redbreast
And brought her cake and wine.

"Eat well of my cake, Jenny,
Drink well of my wine."
"Thank you, Robin, kindly,
You shall be mine."

Jenny she got well,
And stood upon her feet,
And told Robin plainly
She loved him not a bit.

Robin being angry,
Hopped upon a twig,
Saying, "Out upon you! Fie upon you!
Bold-faced jig!"
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Old Woman And The Pedlar
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Bobby Snooks
text:
Little Bobby Snooks was fond of his books,
And loved by his usher and master;
But naughty Jack Spry, he got a black eye,
And carries his nose in a plaster.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: I Saw A Ship A-Sailing
text:
I saw a ship a-sailing,
A-sailing on the sea;
And, oh! it was all laden
With pretty things for thee!

There were comfits in the cabin,
And apples in the hold;
The sails were made of silk,
And the masts were made of gold.

The four-and-twenty sailors
That stood between the decks,
Were four-and-twenty white mice
With chains about their necks.

The captain was a duck,
With a packet on his back;
And when the ship began to move,
The captain said, "Quack! Quack!"
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: A Walnut
text:
As soft as silk, as white as milk,
As bitter as gall, a strong wall,
And a green coat covers me all.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: One, He Loves
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Bat, Bat
text:
Bat, bat,
Come under my hat,
And I'll give you a slice of bacon;
And when I bake
I'll give you a cake
If I am not mistaken.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)

title: Hark! Hark!
text:
Hark, hark! the dogs do bark!
Beggars are coming to town:
Some in jags, and some in rags,
And some in velvet gown.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Hart
text:
The hart he loves the high wood,
The hare she loves the hill;
The Knight he loves his bright sword,
The Lady--loves her will.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Man Of Bombay
text:
There was a fat man of Bombay,
Who was smoking one sunshiny day;
When a bird called a snipe
Flew away with his pipe,
Which vexed the fat man of Bombay.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Poor Old Robinson Crusoe!
text:
Poor old Robinson Crusoe!
Poor old Robinson Crusoe!
They made him a coat
Of an old Nanny goat.
I wonder why they should do so!
With a ring-a-ting-tang,
And a ring-a-ting-tang,
Poor old Robinson Crusoe!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: A Sieve
text:
A riddle, a riddle, as I suppose,
A hundred eyes and never a nose!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: My Maid Mary
text:
My maid Mary she minds the dairy,
While I go a-hoeing and mowing each morn;
Gaily run the reel and the little spinning wheel,
While I am singing and mowing my corn.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Pretty John Watts
text:
Pretty John Watts,
We are troubled with rats.
Will you drive them out of the house?
We have mice, too, in plenty,
That feast in the pantry,
But let them stay
And nibble away,
What harm in a little brown mouse?
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: I Love Sixpence
text:
I love sixpence, a jolly, jolly sixpence,
I love sixpence as my life;
I spent a penny of it, I spent a penny of it,
I took a penny home to my wife.

Oh, my little fourpence, a jolly, jolly fourpence,
I love fourpence as my life;
I spent twopence of it, I spent twopence of it,
And I took twopence home to my wife.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Bye, Baby Bunting
text:
Bye, baby bunting,
Father's gone a-hunting,
Mother's gone a-milking,
Sister's gone a-silking,
And brother's gone to buy a skin
To wrap the baby bunting in.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Tom, Tom, The Piper'S Son
text:
Tom, Tom, the piper's son,
Stole a pig, and away he run,
The pig was eat,
And Tom was beat,
And Tom ran crying down the street.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Comical Folk
text:
In a cottage in Fife
Lived a man and his wife
Who, believe me, were comical folk;
For, to people's surprise,
They both saw with their eyes,
And their tongues moved whenever they spoke!

When they were asleep,
I'm told, that to keep
Their eyes open they could not contrive;
They both walked on their feet,
And 'twas thought what they eat
Helped, with drinking, to keep them alive!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Three Sons
text:
There was an old woman had three sons,
Jerry and James and John,
Jerry was hanged, James was drowned,
John was lost and never was found;
And there was an end of her three sons,
Jerry and James and John!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Blacksmith
text:
"Robert Barnes, my fellow fine,
Can you shoe this horse of mine?"
"Yes, good sir, that I can,
As well as any other man;
There's a nail, and there's a prod,
Now, good sir, your horse is shod."
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: One, Two, Buckle My Shoe
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Cock-A-Doodle-Do!
text:
Cock-a-doodle-do!
My dame has lost her shoe,
My master's lost his fiddle-stick
And knows not what to do.

Cock-a-doodle-do!
What is my dame to do?
Till master finds his fiddle-stick,
She'll dance without her shoe.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Pairs Or Pears
text:
Twelve pairs hanging high,
Twelve knights riding by,
Each knight took a pear,
And yet left a dozen there.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Old King Cole
text:
Old King Cole
Was a merry old soul,
And a merry old soul was he;
He called for his pipe,
And he called for his bowl,
And he called for his fiddlers three!
And every fiddler, he had a fine fiddle,
And a very fine fiddle had he.
"Twee tweedle dee, tweedle dee," went the fiddlers.
Oh, there's none so rare
As can compare
With King Cole and his fiddlers three.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)

title: See, See
text:
See, see! What shall I see?
A horse's head where his tail should be.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Dapple-Gray
text:
I had a little pony,
His name was Dapple-Gray,
I lent him to a lady,
To ride a mile away.
She whipped him, she slashed him,
She rode him through the mire;
I would not lend my pony now
For all the lady's hire.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: A Well
text:
As round as an apple, as deep as a cup,
And all the king's horses can't fill it up.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Coffee And Tea
text:
Molly, my sister and I fell out,
And what do you think it was all about?
She loved coffee and I loved tea,
And that was the reason we couldn't agree.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Pussy-Cat Mew
text:
Pussy-cat Mew jumped over a coal,
And in her best petticoat burnt a great hole.
Poor Pussy's weeping, she'll have no more milk
Until her best petticoat's mended with silk.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Dreams
text:
Friday night's dream, on Saturday told,
Is sure to come true, be it never so old.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: A Cock And Bull Story
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Myself
text:
As I walked by myself,
And talked to myself,
Myself said unto me:
"Look to thyself,
Take care of thyself,
For nobody cares for thee."

I answered myself,
And said to myself
In the selfsame repartee:
"Look to thyself,
Or not look to thyself,
The selfsame thing will be."
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Over The Water
text:
Over the water, and over the sea,
And over the water to Charley,
I'll have none of your nasty beef,
Nor I'll have none of your barley;
But I'll have some of your very best flour
To make a white cake for my Charley.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Kilkenny Cats
text:
There were once two cats of Kilkenny.
Each thought there was one cat too many;
So they fought and they fit,
And they scratched and they bit,
Till, excepting their nails,
And the tips of their tails,
Instead of two cats, there weren't any.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Old Grimes
text:
Old Grimes is dead, that good old man,
We ne'er shall see him more;
He used to wear a long brown coat
All buttoned down before.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: A Week Of Birthdays
text:
Monday's child is fair of face,
Tuesday's child is full of grace,
Wednesday's child is full of woe,
Thursday's child has far to go,
Friday's child is loving and giving,
Saturday's child works hard for its living,
But the child that's born on the Sabbath day
Is bonny and blithe, and good and gay.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: A Chimney
text:
Black within and red without;
Four corners round about.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Ladybird
text:
Ladybird, ladybird, fly away home!
Your house is on fire, your children all gone,
All but one, and her name is Ann,
And she crept under the pudding pan.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Around The Green Gravel
text:
Around the green gravel the grass grows green,
And all the pretty maids are plain to be seen;
Wash them with milk, and clothe them with silk,
And write their names with a pen and ink.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Intery, Mintery
text:
Intery, mintery, cutery corn,
Apple seed and apple thorn;
Wire, brier, limber-lock,
Five geese in a flock,
Sit and sing by a spring,
O-u-t, and in again.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Caesar'S Song
text:
Bow-wow-wow!
Whose dog art thou?
Little Tom Tinker's dog,
Bow-wow-wow!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: As I Was Going Along
text:
As I was going along, along,
A-singing a comical song, song, song,
The lane that I went was so long, long, long,
And the song that I sang was so long, long, long,
And so I went singing along.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Hector Protector
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Billy, Billy
text:
"Billy, Billy, come and play,
While the sun shines bright as day."

"Yes, my Polly, so I will,
For I love to please you still."

"Billy, Billy, have you seen
Sam and Betsy on the green?"

"Yes, my Poll, I saw them pass,
Skipping o'er the new-mown grass."

"Billy, Billy, come along,
And I will sing a pretty song."
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Rock-A-Bye, Baby
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Little Jack Horner
text:
Little Jack Horner
Sat in the corner,
Eating of Christmas pie:
He put in his thumb,
And pulled out a plum,
And said, "What a good boy am I!"
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Bird Scarer
text:
Away, birds, away!
Take a little and leave a little,
And do not come again;
For if you do,
I will shoot you through,
And there will be an end of you.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Mary, Mary, Quite Contrary
text:
Mary, Mary, quite contrary,
How does your garden grow?
Silver bells and cockle-shells,
And pretty maids all of a row.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose or the Old Nursery Rhymes, ill. Kate Greenaway (Warne) (1881)
Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Bessy Bell And Mary Gray
text:
Bessy Bell and Mary Gray,
They were two bonny lasses;
They built their house upon the lea,
And covered it with rushes.

Bessy kept the garden gate,
And Mary kept the pantry;
Bessy always had to wait,
While Mary lived in plenty.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Needles And Pins
text:
Needles and pins, needles and pins,
When a man marries his trouble begins.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Mary'S Canary
text:
Mary had a pretty bird,
Feathers bright and yellow,
Slender legs--upon my word
He was a pretty fellow!

The sweetest note he always sung,
Which much delighted Mary.
She often, where the cage was hung,
Sat hearing her canary.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)

title: The Little Bird
text:
Once I saw a little bird
Come hop, hop, hop;
So I cried, "Little bird,
Will you stop, stop, stop?"

And was going to the window
To say, "How do you do?"
But he shook his little tail,
And far away he flew.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Birds Of A Feather
text:
Birds of a feather flock together,
And so will pigs and swine;
Rats and mice will have their choice,
And so will I have mine.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: The Dusty Miller
text:
Margaret wrote a letter,
Sealed it with her finger,
Threw it in the dam
For the dusty miller.
Dusty was his coat,
Dusty was the siller,
Dusty was the kiss
I'd from the dusty miller.
If I had my pockets
Full of gold and siller,
I would give it all
To my dusty miller.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: A Star
text:
Higher than a house, higher than a tree.
Oh! whatever can that be?
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: The Ten O'Clock Scholar
text:
A diller, a dollar, a ten o'clock scholar!
What makes you come so soon?
You used to come at ten o'clock,
But now you come at noon.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Cock-A-Doodle-Do
text:
Oh, my pretty cock, oh, my handsome cock,
I pray you, do not crow before day,
And your comb shall be made of the very beaten gold,
And your wings of the silver so gray.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Old Woman Of Leeds
text:
There was an old woman of Leeds,
Who spent all her time in good deeds;
She worked for the poor
Till her fingers were sore,
This pious old woman of Leeds!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: The Boy In The Barn
text:
A little boy went into a barn,
And lay down on some hay.
An owl came out, and flew about,
And the little boy ran away.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Sunshine
text:
Hick-a-more, Hack-a-more,
On the King's kitchen door,
All the King's horses,
And all the King's men,
Couldn't drive Hick-a-more, Hack-a-more,
Off the King's kitchen door.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Tongs
text:
Long legs, crooked thighs,
Little head, and no eyes.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Jack Jingle
text:
Little Jack Jingle, He used to live single;
But when he got tired of this kind of life,
He left off being single and lived with his wife.
Now what do you think of little Jack Jingle?
Before he was married he used to live single.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Quarrel
text:
My little old man and I fell out;
I'll tell you what 'twas all about,--
I had money and he had none,
And that's the way the noise begun.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: The Pumpkin-Eater
text:
Peter, Peter, pumpkin-eater,
Had a wife and couldn't keep her;
He put her in a pumpkin shell,
And there he kept her very well.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: That'S All
text:
There was an old woman sat spinning,
And that's the first beginning;

She had a calf,
And that's half;

She took it by the tail,
And threw it over the wall,
And that's all!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Bedtime
text:
The Man in the Moon looked out of the moon,
Looked out of the moon and said,
"'Tis time for all children, on the earth
To think about getting to bed!"
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Dance, Little Baby
text:
Dance, little Baby, dance up high!
Never mind, Baby, Mother is by.
Crow and caper, caper and crow,
There, little Baby, there you go!
Up to the ceiling, down to the ground,
Backwards and forwards, round and round;
Dance, little Baby and Mother will sing,
With the merry coral, ding, ding, ding!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Pease Porridge
text:
Pease porridge hot,
Pease porridge cold,
Pease porridge in the pot,
Nine days old.
Some like it hot,
Some like it cold,
Some like it in the pot,
Nine days old.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Crooked Sixpence
text:
There was a crooked man, and he went a crooked mile,
He found a crooked sixpence beside a crooked stile;
He bought a crooked cat, which caught a crooked mouse,
And they all lived together in a little crooked house.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Ducks And Drakes
text:
A duck and a drake,
And a halfpenny cake,
With a penny to pay the old baker.
A hop and a scotch
Is another notch,
Slitherum, slatherum, take her.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Donkey
text:
Donkey, donkey, old and gray,
Ope your mouth and gently bray;
Lift your ears and blow your horn,
To wake the world this sleepy morn.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: If
text:
If all the world were apple pie,
And all the sea were ink,
And all the trees were bread and cheese,
What should we have for drink?
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Bells
text:
"You owe me five shillings,"
Say the bells of St. Helen's.
"When will you pay me?"
Say the bells of Old Bailey.
"When I grow rich,"
Say the bells of Shoreditch.
"When will that be?"
Say the bells of Stepney.
"I do not know,"
Says the great Bell of Bow.
"Two sticks in an apple,"
Ring the bells of Whitechapel.
"Halfpence and farthings,"
Say the bells of St. Martin's.
"Kettles and pans,"
Say the bells of St. Ann's.
"Brickbats and tiles,"
Say the bells of St. Giles.
"Old shoes and slippers,"
Say the bells of St. Peter's.
"Pokers and tongs,"
Say the bells of St. John's.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)
The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)

title: Little Girl And Queen
text:
"Little girl, little girl, where have you been?"
"Gathering roses to give to the Queen."
"Little girl, little girl, what gave she you?"
"She gave me a diamond as big as my shoe."
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: The King Of France
text:
The King of France went up the hill,
With twenty thousand men;
The King of France came down the hill,
And ne'er went up again.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Tarts
text:
The Queen of Hearts,
She made some tarts,
All on a summer's day;
The Knave of Hearts,
He stole the tarts,
And took them clean away.

The King of Hearts
Called for the tarts,
And beat the Knave full sore;
The Knave of Hearts
Brought back the tarts,
And vowed he'd steal no more.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)

title: Come, Let'S To Bed
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Little Maid
text:
"Little maid, pretty maid, whither goest thou?"
"Down in the forest to milk my cow."
"Shall I go with thee?" "No, not now;
When I send for thee, then come thou."
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Bandy Legs
text:
As I was going to sell my eggs
I met a man with bandy legs,
Bandy legs and crooked toes;
I tripped up his heels, and he fell on his nose.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: The Girl And The Birds
text:
When I was a little girl, about seven years old,
I hadn't got a petticoat, to cover me from the cold.
So I went into Darlington, that pretty little town,
And there I bought a petticoat, a cloak, and a gown.
I went into the woods and built me a kirk,
And all the birds of the air, they helped me to work.
The hawk with his long claws pulled down the stone,
The dove with her rough bill brought me them home.
The parrot was the clergyman, the peacock was the clerk,
The bullfinch played the organ,--we made merry work.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Jenny Wren
text:
As little Jenny Wren
Was sitting by her shed.
She waggled with her tail,
And nodded with her head.
She waggled with her tail,
And nodded with her head,
As little Jenny Wren
Was sitting by the shed.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Little Tom Tucker
text:
Little Tom Tucker
Sings for his supper.
What shall he eat?
White bread and butter.
How will he cut it
Without e'er a knife?
How will he be married
Without e'er a wife?
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Multiplication Is Vexation
text:
Multiplication is vexation,
Division is as bad;
The Rule of Three doth puzzle me,
And Practice drives me mad.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Little King Boggen
text:
Little King Boggen, he built a fine hall,
Pie-crust and pastry-crust, that was the wall;
The windows were made of black puddings and white,
And slated with pan-cakes,--you ne'er saw the like!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)

title: Whistle
text:
"Whistle, daughter, whistle;
Whistle, daughter dear."
"I cannot whistle, mammy,
I cannot whistle clear."
"Whistle, daughter, whistle;
Whistle for a pound."
"I cannot whistle, mammy,
I cannot make a sound."
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Bell Horses
text:
Bell horses, bell horses, what time of day?
One o'clock, two o'clock, three and away.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Taffy
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)

title: The Robin
text:
The north wind doth blow,
And we shall have snow,
And what will poor robin do then,
Poor thing?

He'll sit in a barn,
And keep himself warm,
And hide his head under his wing,
Poor thing!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: The Old Woman Of Harrow
text:
There was an old woman of Harrow,
Who visited in a wheelbarrow;
And her servant before,
Knocked loud at each door,
To announce the old woman of Harrow.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Young Roger And Dolly
text:
Young Roger came tapping at Dolly's window,
Thumpaty, thumpaty, thump!

He asked for admittance; she answered him "No!"
Frumpaty, frumpaty, frump!

"No, no, Roger, no! as you came you may go!"
Stumpaty, stumpaty, stump!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: The Coachman
text:
Up at Piccadilly, oh!
The coachman takes his stand,
And when he meets a pretty girl
He takes her by the hand;
Whip away forever, oh!
Drive away so clever, oh!
All the way to Bristol, oh!
He drives her four-in-hand.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: There Was An Old Woman
text:
There was an old woman who lived in a shoe.
She had so many children she didn't know what to do.
She gave them some broth without any bread.
She whipped them all soundly and put them to bed.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: The Old Woman Of Surrey
text:
There was an old woman in Surrey,
Who was morn, noon, and night in a hurry;
Called her husband a fool,
Drove the children to school,
The worrying old woman of Surrey.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: The Little Mouse
text:
I have seen you, little mouse,
Running all about the house,
Through the hole your little eye
In the wainscot peeping sly,
Hoping soon some crumbs to steal,
To make quite a hearty meal.
Look before you venture out,
See if pussy is about.
If she's gone, you'll quickly run
To the larder for some fun;
Round about the dishes creep,
Taking into each a peep,
To choose the daintiest that's there,
Spoiling things you do not care.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Boy And Girl
text:
There was a little boy and a little girl
Lived in an alley;
Says the little boy to the little girl,
"Shall I, oh, shall I?"
Says the little girl to the little boy,
"What shall we do?"
Says the little boy to the little girl,
"I will kiss you."
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose or the Old Nursery Rhymes, ill. Kate Greenaway (Warne) (1881)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: When
text:
When I was a bachelor
I lived by myself;
And all the bread and cheese I got
I laid up on the shelf.

The rats and the mice
They made such a strife,
I was forced to go to London
To buy me a wife.

The streets were so bad,
And the lanes were so narrow,
I was forced to bring my wife home
In a wheelbarrow.

The wheelbarrow broke,
And my wife had a fall;
Down came wheelbarrow,
Little wife and all.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Sing, Sing
text:
Sing, sing, what shall I sing?
Cat's run away with the pudding-string!
Do, do, what shall I do?
The cat has bitten it quite in two.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: London Bridge
text:
London Bridge is broken down,
Dance over my Lady Lee;
London Bridge is broken down,
With a gay lady.

How shall we build it up again?
Dance over my Lady Lee;
How shall we build it up again?
With a gay lady.

Build it up with silver and gold,
Dance over my Lady Lee;
Build it up with silver and gold,
With a gay lady.

Silver and gold will be stole away,
Dance over my Lady Lee;
Silver and gold will be stole away,
With a gay lady.

Build it up with iron and steel,
Dance over my Lady Lee;
Build it up with iron and steel,
With a gay lady.

Iron and steel will bend and bow,
Dance over my Lady Lee;
Iron and steel will bend and bow,
With a gay lady.

Build it up with wood and clay,
Dance over my Lady Lee;
Build it up with wood and clay,
With a gay lady.

Wood and clay will wash away,
Dance over my Lady Lee;
Wood and clay will wash away,
With a gay lady.

Build it up with stone so strong,
Dance over my Lady Lee;
Huzza! 'twill last for ages long,
With a gay lady.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)

title: The Balloon
text:
"What is the news of the day,
Good neighbor, I pray?"
"They say the balloon
Is gone up to the moon!"
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Only True Mother Goose Melodies (Munroe & Francis, Boston) (1833)

title: A Cherry
text:
As I went through the garden gap,
Who should I meet but Dick Red-cap!
A stick in his hand, a stone in his throat,--
If you'll tell me this riddle, I'll give you a groat.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: The Lost Shoe
text:
Doodle doodle doo,
The Princess lost her shoe:
Her Highness hopped,--
The fiddler stopped,
Not knowing what to do.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Hot Codlins
text:
There was a little woman, as I've been told,
Who was not very young, nor yet very old;
Now this little woman her living got
By selling codlins, hot, hot, hot!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Man Of Tobago
text:
There was an old man of Tobago
Who lived on rice, gruel, and sago,
Till much to his bliss,
His physician said this:
"To a leg, sir, of mutton, you may go."
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Ding, Dong, Bell
text:
Ding, dong, bell,
Pussy's in the well!
Who put her in?
Little Tommy Lin.

Who pulled her out?
Little Johnny Stout.
What a naughty boy was that,
To try to drown poor pussy-cat.
Who never did him any harm,
But killed the mice in his father's barn!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Farmer And The Raven
text:
A farmer went trotting upon his gray mare,
Bumpety, bumpety, bump!
With his daughter behind him so rosy and fair,
Lumpety, lumpety, lump!

A raven cried croak! and they all tumbled down,
Bumpety, bumpety, bump!
The mare broke her knees, and the farmer his crown,
Lumpety, lumpety, lump!

The mischievous raven flew laughing away,
Bumpety, bumpety, bump!
And vowed he would serve them the same the next day,
Lumpety, lumpety lump!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)

title: Christmas
text:
Christmas is coming, the geese are getting fat,
Please to put a penny in an old man's hat;
If you haven't got a penny a ha'penny will do,
If you haven't got a ha'penny, God bless you.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Willy Boy
text:
"Willy boy, Willy boy, where are you going?
I will go with you, if that I may."
"I'm going to the meadow to see them a-mowing,
I'm going to help them to make the hay."
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Mouse And The Clock
text:
Hickory, dickory, dock!
The mouse ran up the clock;
The clock struck one,
And down he run,
Hickory, dickory, dock!
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Hot-Cross Buns
text:
Hot-cross Buns!
Hot-cross Buns!
One a penny, two a penny,
Hot-cross Buns!

Hot-cross Buns!
Hot-cross Buns!
If ye have no daughters,
Give them to your sons.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Bobby Shaftoe
text:
Bobby Shaftoe's gone to sea,
With silver buckles on his knee:
He'll come back and marry me,
Pretty Bobby Shaftoe!
Bobby Shaftoe's fat and fair,
Combing down his yellow hair;
He's my love for evermore,
Pretty Bobby Shaftoe.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: The Woman Of Exeter
text:
There dwelt an old woman at Exeter;
When visitors came it sore vexed her,
So for fear they should eat,
She locked up all her meat,
This stingy old woman of Exeter.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)

title: Sneezing
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Pussy-Cat By The Fire
text:
Pussy-cat sits by the fire;
How can she be fair?
In walks the little dog;
Says: "Pussy, are you there?
How do you do, Mistress Pussy?
Mistress Pussy, how d'ye do?"
"I thank you kindly, little dog,
I fare as well as you!"
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)
The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: When The Snow Is On The Ground
text:
The little robin grieves
When the snow is on the ground,
For the trees have no leaves,
And no berries can be found.

The air is cold, the worms are hid;
For robin here what can be done?
Let's strow around some crumbs of bread,
And then he'll live till snow is gone.
source: The Real Mother Goose, ill. Blanche Fisher Wright (Rand McNally)
also_in: Mother Goose, ill. Frederick Richardson (Volland) (1915)

title: Hark! hark! the dogs bark
text:
Hark! hark! the dogs bark,
The beggars are coming to town;
Some in rags and some in tags,
And some in a silken gown.
Some gave them white bread,
And some gave them brown,
And some gave them a good horse-whip,
And sent them out of the town.
source: Mother Goose or the Old Nursery Rhymes, ill. Kate Greenaway (Warne)

title: Little Jack Horner sat in the corner
text:
Little Jack Horner sat in the corner,
Eating a Christmas pie;
He put in his thumb, and pulled out a plum,
And said, oh! what a good boy am I.
source: Mother Goose or the Old Nursery Rhymes, ill. Kate Greenaway (Warne)

title: To market, to market, to buy a plum cake
text:
To market, to market, to buy a plum cake,
Home again, home again, market is late;
To market, to market, to buy a plum bun,
Home again, home again, market is done.
source: Mother Goose or the Old Nursery Rhymes, ill. Kate Greenaway (Warne)

title: Elsie Marley has grown so fine
text:
Elsie Marley has grown so fine,
She won't get up to serve the swine;
But lies in bed till eight or nine,
And surely she does take her time.
source: Mother Goose or the Old Nursery Rhymes, ill. Kate Greenaway (Warne)

title: Daffy-down-dilly has come up to town
text:
Daffy-down-dilly has come up to town,
In a yellow petticoat and a green gown.
source: Mother Goose or the Old Nursery Rhymes, ill. Kate Greenaway (Warne)
also_in: The Nursery Rhymes of England, J. O. Halliwell (1842; Warne edition) (1886)

title: Jack Sprat could eat no fat
text:
Jack Sprat could eat no fat,
His wife could eat no lean;
And so between them both,
They licked the platter clean.
source: Mother Goose or the Old Nursery Rhymes, ill. Kate Greenaway (Warne)
